messages:
ashley: Heads up — after merging autotune-spline-chooser (PR #2483) we see a clear p95 regression on hosted GQA traffic around the 512->520 token boundary. Rolling back in progress but wanted to capture notes here. :grimacing:

khoa: saw it too. p95 up ~12-18% on the GQA test harness. Not GPU saturation — occupancy looks fine. KV cache page churn spikes at the same boundary. My initial profiler snapshot shows a kernel switch + prefetch overhead.

khoa: profiler excerpt:```
# perf summary (averaged over ~1k requests)
seq=508: attn_kernel=gqa_paged_v2   block=32  time=1.05ms  (kv-prefetch hits: 82%)
seq=514: attn_kernel=gqa_paged_v2   block=32  time=1.08ms  (kv-prefetch hits: 79%)
seq=516: attn_kernel=mqa_unified     block=16  time=1.34ms  (kv-prefetch misses: 41%)
seq=520: attn_kernel=mqa_unified     block=16  time=1.45ms  (kv-prefetch misses: 47%)
# note: autotune chose mqa_unified at ~515 based on predicted compute cost
```

maria: That matches my local repro. The spline tuner cost model predicted better throughput for the smaller-block path, but it didn't account for paged KV layout fragmentation and extra prefetch/merge overhead. In short: the kernel pick ignored kv_layout_metric and prefetch penalty.

maria: Options: 1) widen the seqlen hysteresis window (e.g., require delta >= 32 tokens before switching kernels), 2) include kv-fragmentation factor in the cost function (prefetch_penalty * frag_ratio), 3) short-term: force layout-aware fallback for GQA-workloads when frag_ratio > 0.3. I prefer 3 as hotfix.

jen: We can flip a runtime flag and ship a canary to 10% quickly. Suggest flag: KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_FALLBACK=layout_aware or --autotune-fallback=legacy. Can push rollout via console canary and a per-model config override.

ashley: @jen please do the canary. @khoa can you produce a flame trace with KV allocation timelines for obs in the next 30m? That will help decide whether to revert or patch.

perf-bot: automated benchmark summary for PR #2483 (baseline vs pr):```
baseline (main): p50=85ms p95=210ms p99=380ms throughput=250 req/s
pr/2483:        p50=86ms p95=240ms p99=410ms throughput=252 req/s
difference: +14% p95, +8% p99, +0.8% throughput
test details: gqa-mixed (seq 128-1024), block profile weighted toward seq ~512
```

khoa: attaching quick grep of logs that show KV page evictions spiking at the switch point:```
[2026-03-18T10:02:12Z] req_id=abc123 seq=516 kernel=mqa_unified kv_evictions=7 prefetch_misses=3
[2026-03-18T10:02:12Z] req_id=abc125 seq=520 kernel=mqa_unified kv_evictions=9 prefetch_misses=4
[2026-03-18T10:02:13Z] req_id=abc130 seq=508 kernel=gqa_paged_v2   kv_evictions=1 prefetch_misses=0
```

maria: Quick patch I tested locally (very small) — extend autotune cost to include kv_frag factor. Patch snippet:```diff
- score = compute_cost(kernel, seqlen)
+ score = compute_cost(kernel, seqlen) + prefetch_penalty(kernel) * kv_frag_ratio
```
This moves the decision back to gqa_paged_v2 around 514-520 which restores p95 in my runs.

jen: pushed canary with KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_FALLBACK=layout_aware to 10% model traffic. Monitoring APM and perf traces now. Link to canary rollout: https://console.internal/redwood/canaries/2483-canary

ashley: thanks. If canary looks good for 15m we'll either keep the flag or merge maria's cost fix. Prefer long-term fix + added telemetry for kv_frag_ratio in autotune metrics.

khoa: FYI, I believe this is a class of regression where autotune spline transitions across micro-architecture/kernel boundaries cause hidden memory-path costs. We should add a unit test in the autotuner that simulates paged KV fragmentation and asserts kernel stability across small seqlen perturbations.

jen: agreed. created BUG-3421 (autotune: include kv-frag in cost model + add stability test). I'll add the canary graph to the ticket.

ashley: plan for next steps: 1) wait 15m on canary, 2) if stable, merge maria's small patch + add metric; 3) add autotuner unit test and a short-term hysteresis default of 32 tokens.

maria: adding note: this only affected GQA-heavy models; MQA-only workloads didn't regress because their KV layout aligns with small-block kernels. Good reason to keep per-model kv_layout hinting.

ashley: cool. keeping this thread open until resolved. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
